title: I vibe coded a mining game you can play in your browser: Core Echo. Looking for feedback!
author: Beloviiks2

comments.author: maddix_cummings
comments.body:
I find it really sad that so many people are vibe coding concepts and games that have already been done ad nauseam in the past instead of using AI to put a new spin on it.

I don't mean to be harsh but why would I play your game instead of the original Motherload on miniclip or whatever else? The story?

replies.author: Beloviiks2
replies.body:
The most honest answer I could give you is that I wanted to make a game I’d enjoy playing.

I really like games in this genre, especially on mobile, but I haven’t found anything fresh. I’ve finished most of the ones available, and I wanted more.

I have no ambitions of turning this into a business or anything like that, so I just built my own toy

replies.author: Disastrous-Round-150
replies.body: Maybe because you would need to run the original game through a emulator or something similar?! I love seeing old thought through concepts spark to new life through AI game dev especially when people offer it for free!

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body: Motherload which is, as far as I know, the original game is still available on Miniclip and other platforms. And as OP said they themselves have played clones of it.

replies.author: Disastrous-Round-150
replies.body: Diggers on the Amiga came out in 1993, eleven years before Motherload in 2004. Miner on the TRS-80 already had players digging for gold and returning to the surface to sell it in 1980. Motherload may have inspired those particular clones, but it didn’t originate the concept. Being free doesn’t change that.

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body:
What are you even on about? I never said Motherload was the original, I specified "as far as I know". And yes, it most likely inspired Motherload, but in your own words, these clones were then inspired by Motherload. Your point supports my original point, which is that there is no point recreating what has been recreated over and over again when we now have AI to recreated it AND add something to it.

Again, was not my original point and invention does not mean proliferation. And I don't even understand your "being free doesn't change that", change what? You said "especially when it's for free", I pointed out that the original and an overwhelming majority of the clones are already free.

replies.author: Disastrous-Round-150
replies.body: Great games have many clones! 🔥 I love OPs work look like another lovely clone! ❤️

replies.author: PickleCapable3479
replies.body:
Ad nauseam? Or perhaps "Ad Fundum"? 😄 Sorry, I could not resist.
